instructor: Ekrem Baser is a great instructor. Despite it being his first time teaching this course, he did a great job. He comes to the class prepared and explains the statistics behind quantitative methods and how to interpret regression results.  The assignments in this class helped me learn R and run regressions, do plots, and interpret the significance of results, etc. Ekrem Baser is always respectful, never late, and always on time for the class. He is very kind and understanding, keeps the topic interesting, and is good at engaging the class and encouraging students to participate.

He is incredibly respectful towards his students, his material, and his craft overall. He is kind, approachable, helpful, and really interested in helping you learn the material above anything else. And his design of the course, as well as his grading, reflects all these.

He is a grace to the Bilkent IR department, and I mean it.
He should indeed TEACH other "scholars" on how to TEACH, and how to TEACH quantitative stuff. His way of teaching statistics should win a Nobel prize, he knows what he is doing and he really transfers his knowledge onto the students like it is nothing. It is clear that he does not memorize how to do MATH, he analytically decomposes it and makes it functional, so we, the students, also do not lean onto memorizing it and instead learn why and how things happen, he TEACHES us how to USE OUR BRAIN. I am so glad I took this course from him at the beginning of my master's degree, now I can apply quantitative method to all my other papers thanks to this brilliant man!
Also he is very quick-witted and knows the student psyche very well, so adjusts perfectly. One last thing: his English is also great, so his fluency in English almost magically translates to his fluency in teaching math and quant stuff. He is confident and stands firm in his knowledge while teaching. His confidence and proficiency shine through in every class! Long live Ekrem Hoca!

-I have rarely seen an instructor as committed to his students. The instructor showed high levels of care and respect, especially when the student shows interest and hard work in the class and homeworks. He also encouraged students to go beyond their unknown limits and produce quality work.
No weak points, the instructor is a true contribution to Bilkent and to anyone who has the chance to cross his path during their academic career.
course:
I think this course should have been an introduction to quantitative methods. An advanced course is needed. One course in quantitative method is very limited. We could only cover the basics but I would like to learn more advanced stuff too. I would really like to see Ekrem Baser teach a research design course too, I think he would be very good at it and I think we need a research design course in addition to Quantitative Methods I + Quantitative Methods II courses. So please open more courses both for advanced methodologies and research design.

Also, next term I would not recommend this course to be taught one day a week, three hours in a row. Even with a 15 min break, it is a bit difficult to keep focused for three hours.

Although we have all agreed to have 3-hour block lessons at the beginning of the term, and it has its own benefits, I should say that it is also very challenging to focus, especially in the last 30 minutes. Maybe keeping the block lesson style with more break time would be better for future sections.
-The classworks allowed me to practise the different codes on R. I am grateful for this course and for the skills learnt.
The 3-hour lecture was a bit heavy, but made it effective. A suggestion would be to offer more quant courses adapted for political science students, without a strong economics/math background.
assistant: Deniz was just great. His teaching style was effective and confident during tutorials, and he helped with each and every question and problem we had as much as he could in one hour.
Deniz was nice and his tutorials helped.
The TA was a great addition to the course. Whenever I had a question, the TA went beyond his way to give me convincing answers and tips for future work. My favourite course and team for sure!

instructor: Ekrem hoca çok kibar, anlayışlı ve yardımsever bir akademisyen. Dersi anlatma ve öğretirken ufuk açmada başarılı biri.

Ekrem hoca is a very kind instructor who does his best to gauge interest in the subject that is being taught. However, as a graduate student, the Quantitative Methods course felt too much like an introduction to statistics 101 and was beneath the expected levels. While I am certain this has nothing to do with Ekrem Hoca himself, the way the course is being taught and the syllabus need a serious overhaul to facilitate the needs of graduate students.

Even though I enjoy his class, he sometimes rambles on about points that we could skip. He often wants to explain the logic behind everything, but we cannot always remember all of it while we are working through the material. Other than that, I believe he has no major weak points. He is one of the professors who has an open-door policy and is easy to reach.

course: Please refer to question 12.
It is well-organised, informative and applicable course. Just, there is more need to increase the labs because it is the best place to grasp the course materials.

I believe this class is not 100% quantitative because we mostly focus on theory. The application part remains weak, and I cannot fully apply what I learn in R Markdown. We learn the logic behind the methods, but the class is too theoretical. Also, since time is limited, I still believe that methods courses should be taught over two semesters: perhaps one semester for theory and another semester for application. The lab classes were not explanatory enough and did not provide sufficient practice.

Dersin içeriğinin biraz değişmesinin veya dersin ikiye ayrılıp Quant I-II olarak verilmesinin daha iyi olabileceğini düşünüyorum. Sınıftaki herkesin de seviyesi aynı olmayınca basit bir şeye uzun zaman harcayabiliyoruz. Ek olarak lablar pek efektif geçmiyor. TA’imiz çok tatlı bir insandı fakat bence R programına daha hakim olan biri asistanlık yapmalı. Çünkü takıldığımız yerde “chatgpt’ye soralım” gibi anlar oldu ve bunu aslında evde de yapabiliriz. Biraz daha mantığını anlatabilen biriyle. dersle bağlantı kuran bir lab dizayn edilirse çok daha iyi olabileceğini düşünüyorum.
Lab bölümünü ( R öğretmeyi) Ekrem hoca bence yürütmeli.  Asistanı çok iyi niyetli biri olsa da bu kadar kritik bir programı bence akademisyenler öğretmeli
assistant: Dilara çok yardımcı ve güler yüzlüydü.

Dilara did her best to accommodate students during lab sessions. However, she herself was not an experienced TA and remained rather inefficient during lab sessions. After some point, constantly getting "maybe you can ask this the AI" as an answer practically removed the need for further participation in lab sessions, which propmted me to abandon lab hours. The lab sessions themselves need a VERY serious overhaul, just as the course itself needs it too.

The course has a TA, but the only difference between the TA and me is that she took the course only one semester before I did. When I went to lab hours, she copied what she was going to say from her notes and read through them. When I had an error, she told me to ask AI. Another issue is that when I did not understand something, she said, “I don’t know; Ekrem Hoca will teach you in the next class,” and so on. As a suggestion, I think someone who is more capable of using R should lead the lab hours, because in this form, they do not make much sense.
In lab sessions, we learn many things for R program thanks to Dilara.

Ekrem Hoca is open to all questions, even the stupid ones. He does not get tired of explaining the same thing over and over, which was necessary for this course, and I really appreciate it. He is also very kind and has good communication with the students. His teaching skills are amazing. He has no weak points.

His pace is generally very effective when explaining difficult material. He makes a genuine effort to ensure that everyone understands, breaking concepts down into clear, accessible steps and revisiting the intuition when necessary. He also situates the material within broader debates in International Politics and frequently provides relevant scholarly references, which strengthens the course’s intellectual depth.

A minor drawback is that, in order to be certain that no one leaves the classroom with unresolved questions, he sometimes repeats material we have already covered, and this can occasionally constrain how much new content we are able to complete within the allotted time.

Ekrem Hoca her zaman neşesiyle, yardım severliğiyle, anlayışıyla bizlere çok yardımcı oldu. Hiçbir soruyu üstünkörü cevaplamadı, bir sorunu olan kimseyi geri çevirmedi. Oldukça sayısal bir ders olmasına rağmen tüm sınıfa bir şeyler öğretebilmeye çalıştı.
course: There is no any weak aspect but the strongest aspect was the (bi-)weekly take-home assignments, which made me utter and hit "aha" moments of some difficult game models we covered during the class.

The strongest part of the course is that it really teaches you about something and pushes you to be attentive (except you are an ECON student who took this course just to increase your GPA). I am now at least able to understand IR papers that utilize game theory models. However, as a grad student, it took so much of my time with the two midterms, 4 assignments, and a final. If you want to do well in the exams, you should really study for this course from the very beginning; otherwise, you will have a really difficult time as the term progresses. In the end, I've learned a lot but was unable to produce something new, which is usually what a grad student should look for or is expected to do after a class.

In my view, the course has many strengths, so I would mainly highlight one weakness. Given that it is labelled Game Theory and International Politics, it would have been even better if more IR-focused journal articles explicitly integrating game theory were incorporated into the syllabus. That said, I also understand that the course is primarily an introductory, methods-oriented class, so the emphasis on foundations is reasonable. The assignments are well designed for monitoring understanding throughout the semester, and the course would be even stronger if similar assignments were provided on a weekly basis.
